Dry front Sunday, rain chance late next week

east_texas.headline: Sunny and milder today after a frosty start. Near 70 Saturday, then a mostly dry front Sunday.
east_texas.summary: Temperatures dropped to near freezing this morning, with Tyler around 33 and some frost in rural low spots. Southwest winds bring a quick warm-up, with sunny skies and highs in the low to mid 60s this afternoon. Tonight stays much milder, in the upper 40s, with a light southwest breeze. Saturday reaches the low 70s with south winds of 10 to 20 mph. A cold front moves through early Sunday, followed by gusty northwest winds and lows in the 30s Monday morning.
east_texas.rain_note: No rain today or Saturday. A few showers are possible early Sunday, mainly east of I-49, so most of the area stays dry. A storm system from the Southwest could bring a better chance of rain and storms around Thu and Fri, Dec 3 and 4.

days.text: Sunny and milder after a frosty start.
Sunny and warm. South winds 10 to 20 mph.
Cold front early. A few showers possible mainly east of I-49. Gusty northwest winds.

facts.p: SPC: no severe risk through Sunday; watching late next week
No notable outages in Smith or nearby counties
Mid to upper 30s Monday morning, colder in low spots

panels.title: Warm Saturday, dry front Sunday
paras: South winds push highs into the low 70s Saturday. A cold front moves through early Sunday. NWS Shreveport keeps the best shower chances east of I-49, so the Tyler area likely stays dry.
Northwest winds turn gusty behind the front Sunday, and Monday morning drops into the mid to upper 30s. Low spots could come close to freezing, but a widespread freeze is not expected.

panels.title: Warm start to December, rain chance late next week
paras: The Climate Prediction Center strongly favors above-normal temperatures through Dec 10. A storm system from the Southwest is forecast to bring showers and storms around Thu and Fri, Dec 3 and 4, and the Storm Prediction Center says severe potential may increase from the southern Plains into the Southeast.

Most European ensemble members show at least half an inch of rain here Dec 2 to 5, which would help the dry conditions. Timing and amounts are still uncertain. El Niño is very strong and tends to favor an active storm track later in the winter.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Weather Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Tyler airport observations, PowerOutage.us, KLTV closings, Texas A&M Forest Service, Open-Meteo model data (HRRR, NBM, ECMWF, GFS, Canadian).

tables.title: How cold each morning gets
tables.note: In town means Tyler and other built-up areas. Low spots means rural valleys, creek and river bottoms and sandy open fields, which can run 4 to 8 degrees colder on calm, clear nights. Monday morning is the coolest of the next five.

chips.text: Cold Saturday night, teens in high valleys

nm.headline: Mild and mostly sunny today. Strong winds Saturday, a cold Saturday night, then a chance of rain and snow midweek.
nm.summary: High clouds and mild temperatures today, running 5 to 15 degrees above normal, with afternoon breezes over the central highlands. Winds strengthen on peaks and ridges tonight. A fast-moving system brings strong winds Saturday afternoon, with gusts of 35 to 55 mph, highest over the central highlands and the central mountain chain. NWS Albuquerque has High Wind Watches for the central highlands and Union County. Saturday night turns colder, with lows in the teens in the high valleys. Dry weather lasts through Tuesday, then a Pacific low could bring rain and snow to western and central areas Wednesday and Thursday.

days.text: Mostly sunny with high clouds. Breezy over the central highlands.
Strong west to northwest winds, gusts 35 to 55 mph. Turning colder at night.
Sunny and lighter winds. Coldest in the eastern plains.
Dry and breezy to windy, milder.
Dry and mild with breezy southwest winds.

nm.snow_note: Start-of-day readings for Friday. Little change during the dry spell, with some settling at the mid-elevation sites.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu reports 7 inches of new snow in the past week and 15 inches for the season. Resort base depths include man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Strong winds over the highlands
paras: A fast-moving system crosses northern New Mexico Saturday while colder air pushes in from the northeast. NWS Albuquerque expects gusts of 35 to 55 mph Saturday afternoon, highest over the central highlands and the central mountain chain.
Winds stay strong in the northeast through Saturday night. Expect difficult driving for high-profile vehicles, and some weak trees could come down.

panels.title: Teens in the high valleys
paras: Skies clear and winds ease Saturday night. NWS has Angel Fire near 13 and Red River near 18, and enclosed valleys could run colder than forecast if winds go calm.
Angel Fire dropped to about 17 this morning. Protect exposed pipes in unheated buildings.

panels.title: Pacific storm midweek
paras: NWS Albuquerque expects a Pacific low to bring measurable rain and snow to much of western and central New Mexico Wednesday and Thursday, with lighter amounts east of the mountains.

The Climate Prediction Center favors wetter than normal conditions for the Southwest Dec 2 to 10. El Niño is very strong, which tends to favor better snow odds in northern New Mexico as winter goes on.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, Angel Fire airport observations, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, Sipapu snow report, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
